title: Lesson 3: Close Read-aloud, Session 1: Summer Sun Risin'
objective: Students will ask and answer questions about the main character and setting in a story using key details, participate in a song with noun and verb identification, practice a movement routine, and write and draw responses about the story.

what_is_taught.skill: ask questions about a story using key details
answer questions about a story using key details
echo and sing a song line by line while tracking print
generate motions to accompany nouns and verbs in a song
describe story elements such as main character and setting
use pictures and words to write about story elements
participate in partner talk to discuss story elements and reading behaviors

student_actions.recognition_identification: identify nouns and verbs in a song by touching head or foot
student_actions.oral_production: echo song lines, sing song with movements, answer questions orally, participate in partner talk
student_actions.written_production: write and draw about main character and setting on response sheet
student_actions.procedural_application: practice steps of the Sun Movement routine
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain motions for nouns and verbs, describe story elements orally
student_actions.comprehension_response: answer questions about main character and setting using key details from text

evidence.quote: Sing the 'Sun, Moon, and Stars' song, tracking the print with your finger or a pointer.
Tell students you are going to sing the 'Sun, Moon, and Stars' song aloud line by line and as you do, you would like them to:
Tell students that you are slowly going to repeat the song. When they hear or see a noun they can touch their head, and when they see or hear a verb they can touch their foot.
After singing the song and underlining the nouns and verbs invite students to reread the phrases with you:

'What are some hand gestures, motions, or actions that could go along with these nouns and verbs in the song?' (Responses will vary, but may include: lifting their arms to form a circle; twinkling their fingers like stars; etc.)
-Invite students to join you as you practice Steps 1-5, taking 10-15 seconds for each step.
Remind students of the story 'Elvin, the Boy Who Loved the Sky' and what they have learned about why Elvin loves the sun and moon.
Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner:
-Invite students to show a thumbs-up or to touch their head if they are ready to begin writing and drawing about the main character and setting.

Display Summer Sun Risin' response sheet. Point out that this material has two parts. Tell students that today they will complete only Part 1, by writing and drawing about the main character and setting using key details from the text.
-Transition students to their workspaces and invite them to begin working.
-Circulate and support students as necessary. Encourage them to use classroom resources (Word Walls, high-frequency word lists, and alphabet or letter sound combination charts).
Remind students of the work they did thinking about key details relating to the main character and setting in Summer Sun Risin' during the close read-aloud.

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Model reading aloud with expression and fluency; model underlining nouns and verbs in different colors; model thinking aloud about story elements; model cleanup routine; provide positive feedback on student participation and work.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: What are some hand gestures, motions, or actions that could go along with these nouns and verbs in the song?
What does it look like to look closely at the illustrations?
What does it look like to reread the text?
Where does the story take place?
